scope: Newly surfaced build-tool advisory, recorded separately from the original 73 audit findings.

alert.summary: sprintf-js vulnerable to denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers
alert.prerequisite: Attacker control of a format string can supply excessive precision to JavaScript numeric formatting and cause an uncaught RangeError.

locked_dependency.distinction: The separate top-level @electron/get@5.1.0 used by Electron has optional undici rather than global-agent. The affected installed chain is the nested packaging dependency.

exposure_review.observed_use: Build-time artifact downloading and optional proxy logging through app-builder-lib; no imports of these packages were found in application source/build scripts apart from electron-builder packaging configuration and maintenance scripts.
exposure_review.proxy_activation: Nested @electron/get/dist/cjs/index.js calls initializeProxy when ELECTRON_GET_USE_PROXY is truthy. proxy.js requires global-agent only inside initializeProxy; that function is also exported for explicit callers.
exposure_review.logging_activation: Installed roarr/dist/log.js uses a mock logger in Node unless ROARR_LOG is enabled. No environment values were read or recorded.
exposure_review.formatter_calls: roarr/dist/factories/createLogger.js:124,131 invokes sprintf. A lone string message uses fixed %s; context-object calls treat the second argument as the format string.
exposure_review.inspected_callers: All log.trace/debug/info/warn/error calls inspected in global-agent/dist/classes/Agent.js, factories/createProxyController.js, factories/createGlobalProxyAgent.js and routines/bootstrap.js use fixed literal messages. Network URLs, headers, errors and proxy settings are context properties rather than format strings.
exposure_review.conclusion: The affected package is installed for development packaging. No attacker-controlled format-string path was identified in the inspected callers. This is not a universal non-exploitability claim or a reason to mark the advisory fixed.

packaging_review.configured_files: app/electron-builder.yml selects out/** and package.json, with explicit backend/icon/extension extraResources.
packaging_review.dependency_copy: Installed app-builder-lib collects production/optional dependencies separately. Its npm collector runs list with --omit dev; its fallback traversal reads dependencies and optionalDependencies, skipping devDependencies. The affected lock entries are marked dev-only.
packaging_review.inference: The inspected configuration and collector exclude this development-only chain from packaged runtime node_modules. This inference is supported by source/configuration, not a current installer inventory.
packaging_review.local_output_observation: Existing app/out JavaScript/JSON files contain no sprintf-js, roarr or global-agent name matches. Those outputs predate current source and do not certify a current release bundle.
packaging_review.release_artifact: No app/dist packaged artifact was present to inspect. No package/build/install was performed.

checks: Read Dependabot alert 64 through gh api; advisory reports no first patched version.
Read current git HEAD package manifest/lock and installed dependency manifests; inspected chain versions match the lock.
Reviewed formatter, logger, proxy activation and direct installed log call sites.
Searched app/src, app/build, app/scripts and workflow/package configuration for package references.
Reviewed electron-builder file selection and installed production dependency collectors; searched existing local output without rebuilding.

disposition.action_taken: Documentation only; no dependency override, upgrade, source patch or alert dismissal.
disposition.follow_up: Reassess when upstream identifies a patched version or a compatible packaging dependency release removes this chain. Validate any actual dependency change with packaging checks.
limitations: The advisory has no published fixed version in the inspected GitHub response; availability of every possible alternative dependency release was not surveyed.
No exploit was executed and no current release archive was inspected.
The original 73-finding acceptance ledger is unchanged by this separate newly surfaced advisory.
No npm audit, dependency-inventory upload, package installation or network dependency audit was performed.
